arc_title: CRISPR off-target prevalence is assay-dependent
core_claim: A guide RNA's off-target risk can be characterized by a single absolute genome-wide number
evidence_evolution: GUIDE-seq (cell-based, integration tag) reports many sites; CIRCLE-seq (in vitro, sensitive) reports more candidate sites with high false-positive risk; DISCOVER-seq (in vivo, MRE11 ChIP) reports fewer high-confidence sites; CHANGE-seq layers chromatin context on CIRCLE-seq. The 'true' off-target set differs by assay; reconciliation requires assay metadata.

arc_title: Pharmacogenomic reproducibility across cancer cell line panels
core_claim: Drug-response measurements in CCLE and GDSC should be highly correlated for the same drug-cell pairs
evidence_evolution: CCLE (Barretina 2012) and GDSC (Garnett 2012) released parallel pharmacogenomic resources. Haibe-Kains 2013 reported poor IC50 concordance and poor genomic-marker reproducibility. The 2015 consortium harmonization reanalysis showed that concordance improves when AUC-style metrics, matched compounds, and harmonized processing are used; it does not fully overturn the original poor reproducibility of IC50-style measurements.

arc_title: Gut microbiome composition and obesity (Firmicutes/Bacteroidetes ratio)
core_claim: An elevated Firmicutes:Bacteroidetes ratio is a reliable signature of obesity in humans
evidence_evolution: Ley 2005 / Turnbaugh 2006 reported F:B ratio shifts in obese mice and humans. Walters 2014 meta-analysis found weak, inconsistent effect across cohorts. Sze & Schloss 2016 reanalysis of 10 studies found F:B differences were small and not reliably reproducible - the textbook claim no longer holds at population scale.

arc_title: AlphaFold2 accuracy on disordered regions and conformational ensembles
core_claim: AlphaFold2 produces accurate structures for any protein sequence
evidence_evolution: Jumper 2021 reports CASP14-level accuracy for many ordered protein domains. Akdel 2022 is a broad community assessment across applications including drug discovery, complexes, and IDPs. Ruff & Pappu 2021 is the clean IDR-specific source: low pLDDT often marks disorder rather than ordinary structural error. Saldano 2022 shows conformational-diversity limits: AlphaFold often converges to one conformer even where multiple experimentally known states exist.

arc_title: PD-L1 IHC concordance across diagnostic assays in NSCLC
core_claim: PD-L1 expression measured by IHC is a robust predictor of immunotherapy response
evidence_evolution: Blueprint Phase 1 (Hirsch 2017) found three of four assays broadly concordant for tumor-cell PD-L1 scoring, with SP142 lower. Blueprint Phase 2 (Tsao 2018) showed immune-cell scoring varies more strongly across assays and pathologists. Rimm 2017 reported inter-assay and inter-reader variation. The arc is tumor-cell versus immune-cell scope, not a direct flip-flop.

arc_title: BRCA1 missense variants - saturation genome editing reclassification

arc_title: Single-cell RNA-seq batch correction - no universal best method
core_claim: A single batch-correction algorithm is appropriate for all scRNA-seq integration tasks
evidence_evolution: MNN (Haghverdi 2018) and Seurat v3 anchor-based integration (Stuart 2019) introduced popular integration methods. Tran 2020 and Luecken 2022 both found that different methods win in different scenarios; no universal best method exists, and performance depends on cell-type composition imbalance and the trade-off between batch removal and biological conservation.

arc_title: EZH2 / PRC2 - context-dependent oncogene vs tumor suppressor
core_claim: EZH2 acts as an oncogene through PRC2-mediated H3K27 trimethylation
evidence_evolution: Varambally 2002 established EZH2 overexpression as oncogenic driver in prostate cancer. Morin 2010 / Beguelin 2013 found activating Y641 mutations driving GCB-DLBCL and follicular lymphoma. Ernst 2010 reported inactivating EZH2 mutations in MDS/MPN - loss-of-function pathogenic in myeloid disease. EZH2 is therefore lineage-context-dependent: same gene, opposite roles.

curator_notes: Two opposite cancer roles for the same gene - strong contradiction-by-context arc. Excellent for 'when does claim transfer' QA. Expert note: Y641 mutations in DLBCL are gain-of-function on H3K27me3, creating a hypertrimethylated state; this contrasts with loss-of-function mutations in MDS/MPN.

arc_title: Cellular senescence markers - no single specific marker
core_claim: p16INK4a expression alone reliably identifies senescent cells in tissue
evidence_evolution: Sharpless & Sherr 2015 reviewed marker landscape and noted p16 expression in non-senescent contexts (immune cells, stem cells). Hernandez-Segura 2017 found senescence signatures heterogeneous across triggers/cell types - no canonical transcriptional core. Gorgoulis 2019 international consensus: senescence requires multi-marker evidence (SA--gal + p16/p21 + SASP + proliferation arrest), no single marker is sufficient.

source_papers.title: Forging a signature of in vivo senescence
Unmasking Transcriptional Heterogeneity in Senescent Cells

curator_notes: Definition-evolved arc - the field operationally redefined senescence to a multi-marker requirement. Good 'what counts as evidence' QA. Expert note: treat Gorgoulis 2019 as a field-defining consensus statement; p21/CDKN1A is a common companion marker to p16.

arc_title: Triple-negative breast cancer - molecular subtype heterogeneity
core_claim: TNBC (ER-/PR-/HER2-) is a single therapeutic category
evidence_evolution: Lehmann 2011 defined six TNBC subtypes (BL1, BL2, IM, M, MSL, LAR). Burstein 2015 proposed an alternative four-subtype scheme (LAR, MES, BLIS, BLIA) with different gene panels and slightly different patient stratification. Lehmann 2016 refinement removed lymphocyte/stromal-driven subtypes (IM, MSL) as contamination, collapsing to four. Two competing schemas exist; both are improvements over 'TNBC = one disease'.

arc_title: Cu electrode CO2 reduction - product distribution depends on facet/potential/electrolyte
core_claim: Copper produces a fixed product distribution (e.g. methane, ethylene) under CO2 reduction
evidence_evolution: Hori 1994 systematized Cu CO2RR product selectivity in a metal-series context rather than serving as the original hydrocarbon-discovery paper. Hori 2003 showed single-crystal Cu(100) favors C2 products while Cu(111) favors C1 products. Kuhl 2012 quantified many products versus potential on polycrystalline Cu, and Mistry 2016 showed plasma-activated oxidized Cu can drive ethylene selectivity. The quantitative selectivity claim is facet-, potential-, electrolyte-, and treatment-bound.

arc_title: Soai asymmetric autocatalysis - mechanism still debated
core_claim: The Soai reaction unambiguously demonstrates a deterministic enantioselective autocatalytic mechanism
evidence_evolution: Soai 1995 reported autocatalytic amplification of ee in alkylation of pyrimidine carbaldehyde. Singleton & Vo 2002 found the reaction can produce high ee from no added chiral influence - apparent stochastic chiral symmetry breaking. Blackmond 2004 proposed a dimer-based kinetic model. Mechanism still partly open; reproducibility constrained by trace chiral contamination control.

arc_title: Cu-zeolite methane-to-methanol active site identity
core_claim: A defined dicopper [Cu2O]2+ core in Cu-ZSM-5 is the universal active site for selective CH4 -> MeOH
evidence_evolution: Groothaert 2005 proposed bis(mu-oxo)dicopper from Cu-ZSM-5/MOR spectroscopy. Woertink 2009 reassigned to mono(mu-oxo) [Cu2O]2+ core via resonance Raman. Grundner 2015 showed Cu-MOR active site is a trinuclear [Cu3(mu-O)3]2+ cluster, not a dicopper core - framework-dependent active species. arc_title: Pd cross-coupling - homogeneous molecular Pd vs heterogeneous nanoparticle active species
core_claim: Pd nanoparticle catalysts in Suzuki/Heck couplings catalyze on the nanoparticle surface
evidence_evolution: Reetz & de Vries 2004 showed ligand-free, very low-Pd Heck reactions proceed via leached Pd species, suggesting molecular catalyst dominates. de Vries 2006 unified mechanism: nanoparticles act as reservoirs releasing active soluble Pd. Phan, Van Der Sluys & Jones 2006 reviewed 'is it heterogeneous?' literature: most reported 'heterogeneous' Pd catalysts are reservoirs for molecular species; true surface catalysis is rare and depends on substrate/temperature.

arc_title: Proline-catalyzed asymmetric aldol - Houk-List mechanism vs alternatives
core_claim: Proline catalyzes asymmetric aldol exclusively via a Houk-List enamine transition state
evidence_evolution: List/Lerner/Barbas 2000 demonstrated proline-catalyzed direct asymmetric aldol. Bahmanyar & Houk 2001/2003 computed enamine transition state predicting stereochemistry - Houk-List model. Schmid/Zeitler/Gschwind 2010 NMR studies of proline enamine intermediates revealed populations and exchange consistent with multiple TS geometries; the simple Houk-List picture is one limit. Mechanism is enamine-based but stereo-determining TS depends on substrate.

Cu surface state (oxidation, roughness, pretreatment) sets nucleation density and grain size - same gas chemistry, different Cu pretreatment, very different graphene quality.

Pretreatment-dependency arc. Good for QA on hidden process variables governing nominally identical recipes. Expert note: Hao 2013 trace surface oxygen on Cu suppresses nucleation density to about 4 nuclei/cm2; this is the mechanistic punchline.

arc_title: Ni-rich NMC layered oxides - energy density vs cycling stability trade-off
core_claim: High-nickel content in LiNixMnyCozO2 cathodes universally improves battery performance
evidence_evolution: Sun 2009 demonstrated concentration-gradient core-shell NMC particles to mitigate Ni-rich surface degradation. Jung 2017 systematically studied oxygen release: increasing Ni content increases capacity but also accelerates oxygen evolution at high SOC, leading to electrolyte oxidation and capacity fade. Manthiram 2016 reviewed Ni-rich and Li-rich layered oxide chemistries summarizing the energy-density vs stability/safety trade-off. Higher Ni is better for energy, worse for life and safety - the optimum depends on application.

arc_title: Halide perovskites - defect tolerance vs ion migration
core_claim: Halide perovskites are 'defect tolerant' so solution-processed films achieve electronic quality near single crystals
evidence_evolution: Stranks 2013 measured electron-hole diffusion lengths >1 mum in solution-processed MAPbI3 films, motivating defect-tolerance narrative. Yin 2014 first-principles work formalized 'defect tolerance' (shallow rather than deep defect states for dominant native defects). Snaith 2014 documented anomalous J-V hysteresis in PSCs, attributed to mobile ions. Yuan & Huang 2016 reviewed halide ion migration as a major source of hysteresis, photoinstability, and operational degradation. Defect tolerance is partially correct for electronic recombination, but ion migration is a separate active failure mode.
